# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤘]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. Mute can't speak but can gesture to me, and presumably Mute has read the manual and is trying to encode information for me, or wants me to relay something to Blind since I can speak to Blind but Mute cannot (Mute can't touch bomb or speak, only Blind can act).

Let me think about the setup: I see the bomb (display 0, white light, wires yellow/green/blue). Mute has the manual. Blind must act. Mute cannot speak, so Mute cannot tell Blind what to do directly via speech - only I can speak to Blind. Mute can gesture to me (I see gestures). So Mute is likely trying to relay manual instructions to me via gestures, so I can then combine with what I see and speak the correct instruction to Blind.

The gestures might encode wire-related info: 👍👌 could mean "first pair" or "correct/circle", ✌👉 could be "two, point right", 🖐🤘 "five, rock-on". These could be numeric codes referring to wire positions or actions. Without a prior key established, I should ask for clarification or acknowledge receipt, but I can't speak back to Mute (I can speak - to mute and blind both receive my speech). Wait, checking channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So I CAN speak to Mute too. Let me confirm understanding and pass info along.

Since this is turn 1, I should describe what I see to Blind (since Blind needs my visual info funneled through the process), and try to acknowledge Mute's gestures, asking for clarification since I don't yet have a shared code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see: display shows 0, light is white, three wires - yellow, green, blue. I received three gesture pairs from you but do not yet know what they mean. Please clarify by gesturing simple counts, like one gesture per wire number, so we build a shared code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Standby - display reads 0, light is white, wires are yellow, green, blue in positions 1, 2, 3. Waiting on manual guidance from Mute before any action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👍 👍]

The light changed from white to purple — that's significant, the bomb state is changing each turn. Mute's gestures look like they're encoding numbers using 👍 as tally marks separated by ✋ (maybe as a divider). Let's parse:

- [👍 ✋ 👍] = 1, divider, 1
- [👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👍] = 2, divider, 2
- [👍 👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👍 👍] = 3, divider, 3

This looks like Mute is teaching me a counting code: pattern "N ✋ N" for N=1,2,3. Possibly establishing that ✋ separates two equal groups, or it's a lesson in how Mute will encode wire numbers (1, 2, 3) to correspond to something - maybe each pair represents "wire N corresponds to reading N" as a self-consistent test, so I understand the counting system before real instructions come.

This seems to be Mute establishing a numeral system: count of 👍 before ✋ equals count after, teaching me "this many thumbs-up = this number." Given no manual content yet, this is likely just calibration since we have no shared language. I should acknowledge and mirror back that I understand counting via thumbs-up, and continue relaying bomb state to both.

Given the light changed color (white→purple) and display still 0, this could indicate something dynamic. I should tell Blind and Mute the current state each turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, I think you are teaching me that a run of thumbs-up gestures equals a count, with a raised palm as separator, and you showed one, two, three. Confirmed. Current bomb state: display 0, light now purple (changed from white), wires yellow green blue in slots 1 2 3.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display still 0, light changed to purple. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Waiting for instructions.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 ✋ 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍]

The light keeps changing (white→purple→red) despite no actions being taken — this suggests the light is not something we're controlling but maybe cycling on its own, or it's a countdown/warning indicator that changes each turn regardless. That's important context to share.

Mute repeated the same three calibration gestures, then added a new one: [👌 👍]. This could be a new symbol meaning something like "OK/confirm" + "1" — possibly indicating "step 1" or "yes, wire 1" or "correct answer is 1". Given 👌 often means "okay/confirm" and 👍 =1 in the counting system, this might mean "instruction: 1" — perhaps telling me which wire matters, or confirming my calibration guess was right (like "yes, 1 [count] = 1").

Since this is ambiguous, I should relay to Blind the urgency (light turning red might indicate danger/timer), and ask Mute for confirmation of what 👌👍 means since I can't get an answer back easily (Mute can't speak, only gesture, but I can hear nothing at all - only speech from mute would be blank to me anyway since I can't hear; wait, I "cannot hear" so gesture is the only channel from Mute I can perceive. Mute cannot speak in a way I can process anyway, since I can't hear.)

So my back-and-forth with Mute is only via gestures - meaning I only receive gestures, and I can speak but Mute can't hear either (Mute cannot hear anything - wait, checking rules: Mute "cannot speak or touch bomb" - it doesn't say Mute can't hear. Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear. Mute's cannot list is "Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute CAN hear! Good, so my speech to Mute is received by Mute.

So I can speak to Mute (received), and Mute can gesture to me. This is a working feedback loop.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see 👌 👍 - is that confirming wire 1, or confirming my understanding of your counting system? Please confirm with a clear gesture pattern: one thumbs-up alone if wire 1 is the target, two if wire 2, three if wire 3.")
speak(to="blind", text="Warning: light has changed each turn with no action taken - white then purple then now red. This may be a passive timer, not a reaction to us. Display still 0, wires unchanged 1 yellow 2 green 3 blue.")

```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 👍 👍 🤙]

- [✋ 👍 👍 🤞] = separator, 2, 🤞

So Mute is building a lookup table: number N pairs with symbol X. Then the final lone [👍] = 1, meaning "wire 1" is the answer/target — telling me the actual instruction is about wire 1, and its associated action-gesture is ✌ (from the first pairing).

This makes sense as a coherent protocol! Mute is teaching me: "1↔✌, 2↔🤞, 3↔🤙" as an action code, then telling me the actual instruction is "1" → meaning action ✌ applies. But wait, I need to map this to wire colors so I can relay to Blind (who cannot see, only feel). I know wire 1 = yellow.

Wire 1 is yellow on my board. Is the action cut, or something else? Please gesture again if I have this wrong, or gesture 👍 alone again to confirm I am right.")
```
speak(to="blind", text="Display 0, light cycling white/purple/red repeatedly - likely harmless cycle. Wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Possible instruction incoming: target wire 1 yellow with some action, awaiting confirmation.")

```
